subject: Literacy
title: Retelling with props
objectives: Children will retell a short story using props or puppets.
Children will use words such as first, then and the end.
content: Telling a story with props, retelling it in their own words, and using puppets with the story.
teachingActivities: Use the same story all week; place props in a story box; use first, then and the end naturally; give children props and let them tell the story their way; accept words, gestures and actions.
learnerActivities: Retell a short story using props or puppets and use story words such as first, then and the end.
resources: A story box with a toy hen, a toy egg, a toy chick and a toy cat
assessment: Observe whether each child retells part of a story with props and uses a story word.
expectedOutcomes: Retells part of a story with props.

lessons.title: The little hen story
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will listen to a short story told with props.
successCriteria: Points to a prop when named
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen to a short story and join in a repeated line; many can name pictures in a book.
resources: A toy hen, egg, chick and cat
lessons.starter: Take the hen from the story box and say "This is Hen. Hen has a secret in her nest."
teacherActivities: Tell the story: "First, Hen sat on her nest. Then she laid an egg. Then crack! Out came a chick. The end." Use each prop as you tell it.
Ask "Who sat on the nest?" and "What came out?"
Tell the story again and let children help move the props.
learnerActivities: Children listen and watch the props.
Children point to the hen and the chick.
Child moves a prop at the right time.
Children say "the end".
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the story: "First, Hen sat on her nest. Then she laid an egg. Then crack! Out came a chick. The end." Use each prop as you tell it. Children: Children listen and watch the props.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Who sat on the nest?" and "What came out?" Children: Children point to the hen and the chick.
Step 3. Teacher: Tell the story again and let children help move the props. Children: Child moves a prop at the right time.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "The end" together. Children: Children say "the end".

practical.title: Story box
steps: Put the props in a story box.
Take them out one at a time as you tell the story.
Pass the props round so each child holds one.
practical.safety: Use large soft props that cannot be swallowed. Supervise handling and do not allow children to put props in mouths.

differentiation.support: Hold the prop together and move it in time with the story.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell what happened first.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What came out of the egg?

expectedOutcomes: Listens to a story with props
Names or points to the props
lessons.conclusion: Put the props back in the box and say "The end."
lessons.homeConnection: Tell a short story at home with two toys and let your child move them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "listen to a short story told with props" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: First, then, the end
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will use the words first, then and the end to retell the story.
successCriteria: Says or signs first, then or the end
Points to the props in order
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen to a short story and join in a repeated line; many can name pictures in a book.
lessons.starter: Hold up the three cards and say "First, then, the end. This is the order of our story."
teacherActivities: Put the three cards on the floor in order and point as you say first, then, the end.
Tell the story again with the cards and ask "What came first?"
Ask "What happened then?" and "What happened at the end?"
Let each child pick up a card and say its story word.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the words.
Child points to the first card.
Child points to the cards.
Child holds up a card and says first, then or end.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the three cards on the floor in order and point as you say first, then, the end. Children: Children look and say the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Tell the story again with the cards and ask "What came first?" Children: Child points to the first card.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What happened then?" and "What happened at the end?" Children: Child points to the cards.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick up a card and say its story word. Children: Child holds up a card and says first, then or end.

practical.title: Story steps
steps: Put three cards on the floor in a row.
Children stand on each card as the story moves along.
Say first, then, the end together.
practical.safety: Use big soft cards on a clear floor. Keep children well apart and supervise movement.

differentiation.support: Point to each card and say the word for the child to copy.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put the cards in order alone.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Puts cards in order with support
lessons.homeConnection: Use the words first, then and the end when you tell stories at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use the words first, then and the end to retell the story" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Puppets tell the story
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will use puppets to tell part of the story.
successCriteria: Moves a puppet for the story
Says a word as the puppet speaks
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen to a short story and join in a repeated line; many can name pictures in a book.
lessons.starter: Make the hen puppet say "Cluck, cluck. I am Hen." Ask "Who is this?"
teacherActivities: Use the hen puppet to tell the first part of the story.
Give the chick puppet to a child and ask them to make it say "cheep".
Retell the story together with two puppets.
Let pairs of children tell the story to each other.
learnerActivities: Children watch and listen.
Child makes the chick say cheep.
Children move puppets and say words.
Child speaks for a puppet.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Use the hen puppet to tell the first part of the story. Children: Children watch and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Give the chick puppet to a child and ask them to make it say "cheep". Children: Child makes the chick say cheep.
Step 3. Teacher: Retell the story together with two puppets. Children: Children move puppets and say words.
Step 4. Teacher: Let pairs of children tell the story to each other. Children: Child speaks for a puppet.

practical.title: Puppet show
steps: Set up a small stage with a cloth nest.
Tell the story with the puppets together.
practical.safety: Check that puppets are clean and have no loose parts. Supervise sharing and keep puppets from mouths.

differentiation.support: Move the puppet together and say the words with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make up a new line for the puppet.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Uses puppets to retell part of a story
Speaks for a puppet with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the puppets to bed and say goodnight.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a puppet from a sock at home and let your child tell a story with it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use puppets to tell part of the story" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Tell it in my own way
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will retell the story in their own words or actions.
successCriteria: Retells at least one part of the story
Uses a prop or an action
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen to a short story and join in a repeated line; many can name pictures in a book.
lessons.starter: Sit on the storyteller’s cushion and say "Who can tell our hen story?"
teacherActivities: Invite a child to sit on the storyteller’s cushion and choose a prop.
Add the child’s words to the story and tell it back to them.
Let two or three children each tell a part.
learnerActivities: Child chooses a prop.
Child says a word or shows an action.
Child listens and nods.
Child tells a part and the group claps.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Invite a child to sit on the storyteller’s cushion and choose a prop. Children: Child chooses a prop.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What happened first?" and wait. Children: Child says a word or shows an action.
Step 3. Teacher: Add the child’s words to the story and tell it back to them. Children: Child listens and nods.
Step 4. Teacher: Let two or three children each tell a part. Children: Child tells a part and the group claps.

practical.title: Storyteller’s cushion
steps: Place a cushion in the circle.
A child sits and tells part of the story with a prop.
The group claps and the next child sits.
practical.safety: Never make a child perform if they do not want to. Accept a gesture or a single word.

differentiation.support: Hold the prop together and offer the first word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell the whole story with first, then and the end.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What happened in the story?
questions.expected: Any part of the story in words or actions.

lessons.conclusion: Clap for all the storytellers and put the props away.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to tell you a story and listen.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "retell the story in their own words or actions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 retelling check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child retells a story with props.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen to a short story and join in a repeated line; many can name pictures in a book.
lessons.starter: Show the story box and three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: props, picture cards and puppets.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child retells with a prop or gesture.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: props, picture cards and puppets. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What happened?" Children: Child retells with a prop or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Story stations
practical.safety: Supervise props closely and keep floors clear. Use large soft props only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and offer two props.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell the story to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: retells part of the story; uses first, then or the end; speaks for a puppet.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
Retells part of a story with props
lessons.homeConnection: Tell stories with toys at home and use the words first, then and the end.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child retells a story with props" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
